import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 653

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/653](https://www.erdosproblems.com/653)
-/

open Finset EuclideanGeometry Filter

namespace Erdos653

/-- Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_653 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (1 - o n) * n ≤ maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n := by
  sorry

end Erdos653

reformulations.difference: Uses a natural-number supremum of attainable counts rather than a literal maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each n, n-element subsets of the plane exist, and each attainable count #(X.image (distinctDistancesFrom X)) is at most n. Thus the set of counts is nonempty and bounded in ℕ, so its supremum is attained and equals its maximum. The scratch file proves attainment and the equivalence k ≤ maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n ↔ ∃ X, X.card = n ∧ k ≤ (X.image (distinctDistancesFrom X)).card.

reformulations.difference: Expands the source's g(n) ≥ (1−o(1))n into an existential real error sequence satisfying little-o of 1 and an eventual lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's o =o[atTop] 1 is exactly o(n) → 0. Since g(n) ≤ n, the eventual lower bound gives 1−o(n) ≤ g(n)/n ≤ 1 for positive n, hence g(n)/n → 1. Conversely, that limit supplies o(n) = 1−g(n)/n. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file. No positivity hypothesis on o is missing: eventual nonnegativity follows from the bound and g(n) ≤ n.
